about: MUTATING (removes only the restore drill's own scratch objects, and only once the drill has finished and its logs are on this request; READ-ONLY to the system of record) — READS the restore drill that drill-gcs-restore started, the second half of the drill David asked for on 2026-11-14 ~15:40Z before the Postgres move (backlog 156eb6e5; design 3c475a19 car 4). Split off by backlog a1cbd16c after the first real run, ops-request 24fd49e7, held the forge's single ops-runner lane 47 minutes waiting on the Job and then removed the Job, its claim and its ConfigMap without the restore log, which the Job controller had deleted with the pod on DeadlineExceeded; the record could not say how far the 7.5 GB dump got. It is the same script, infra/forge/drill-gcs-restore.sh, with the literal --read — one definition of the bounds, the reads and the removal. Takes no arguments. It reads Job boss/boss-restore-drill (named AND labelled app=boss-restore-drill; anything else is refused, exit 78, and never touched) and answers one of four ways. NO DRILL: says so and refuses (exit 78), nothing removed. RUNNING: prints STILL RUNNING with the uid, the start time, the seconds elapsed, the pod and its node, both deadlines, and the last 40 lines of each container's log — the restore container's progress line every 60 s carries the elapsed seconds, the scratch database's pg_database_size and the statement running — then exits 75, the not-yet, and REMOVES NOTHING. FINISHED (Complete or Failed — including the restore ending itself at its inner deadline, which leaves a Failed pod the controller keeps): prints both containers' WHOLE logs, the scratch claim's Longhorn replicas (node and disk path) and the Job's own run time, and says out loud when no pod stands (a DeadlineExceeded backstop deletes it) — all BEFORE anything is removed; then removes the Job by its uid (DeleteOptions preconditions.uid, Foreground), the pod, the ephemeral claim and the ConfigMap going with it by garbage collection, all three read back gone. CANNOT START: a pod waiting on ErrImagePull, ImagePullBackOff, InvalidImageName or CreateContainer(Config)Error 900 s after it was made has run nothing and has no log to lose, so it is removed the same way rather than left to the 18000 s backstop. THE VERDICT, for a finished drill: the fetch receipt verified the dump it kept; the pod exited 0 on the data node (boss.dev/purpose=database, read again); every Longhorn replica of the claim sits on that node at /var/mnt/postgres; the dump restored at least one audit row; dump <= live on audit_log, jobs, steps and the newest audit id (live runs ahead by the hours since the 09:10Z dump); the live log holds exactly one row at the dump's newest audit id; and the scratch objects read back gone. The ops-request records one `receipt:` JSON line (the dump's object, stamp, generation and sha256, both sides' four counts, the placement, the restore's measured restore_seconds and restored_bytes and the Job's job_seconds — the numbers the next sizing of the deadlines reads — and the removal), then the effect line, which carries the restore's seconds and bytes. NO PASSKEY, for drill-gcs-restore's reasons: no packet-supplied word at all; the only write is the delete, by uid, of the tree's own Job that its own start created; and a plan would render nothing an approver could judge. TIMEOUT 600: the door's first-time image pull (120 s), a dozen kubectl reads and two container logs bounded at 20 s, and one removal read back for up to 300 s; it waits on nothing the drill does. Pinned by crates/core/boss-testing/tests/drill_gcs_restore_sh.rs.
effect: ^read-restore-drill: RESTORED dump [^ ]+[.]sql[.]gz \(sha256 [0-9a-f]{64}\) into a scratch database on the postgres disk of [a-z0-9-]+ in [0-9]+s \([0-9]+ bytes restored\) — dump <= live on audit_log, jobs and steps \(audit_log [0-9]+/[0-9]+, jobs [0-9]+/[0-9]+, steps [0-9]+/[0-9]+\); newest audit id [0-9]+ present in the live system of record; scratch Job and claim removed and read back gone$
